restrictions: Ordinary collision of SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps from the standard IV: two 128-byte messages with the same random first block M0 and second blocks M1, M1' = M1 + DL (differences in words 8..12), then the common padding block. The second block is the transplanted advice pair with A[6], A[7] released over a list generated at import by rule on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe: 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes, 3,462,264 (a2, W10) keys; the walk constants c9, C9 are shifted by 0x05cefde0. The W17 condition is solved per F9 claw by a generic bit-sliced pass over the 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes; a passing prefix is completed, tested on scalar words and, at a key hit, expanded to the classes of its group.

Refiles 9a255e58 with the joint mate experiment its review asked for (0 of 9,129 F8-passing mates of 25,221 verified tail hits followed the advice differences past row 19). Otherwise the model of our 0b62ed88 (keys-only, valid at 94.4431). Our w13 program, list re-based to a new fibre and generated by rule. Trials are F8-passing entries (mate model of a7b383d1, credited): 10598.2 per distinct claw, the 99% lower bound of our count on 2,000 F9 claws; every key hit is tested; success by second-order Bonferroni over all hits on the keys' mate-union events, valid for any dependence between hits. Walk table 99,328 slots of 40 bits; walk statistics from 48 full windows of the shipped program. Time 94.1966: work cap (K = 10,719, 1% above its formula; pass 143,633), setup 1,107,473,556 operations, 2^43 preprocessing. Tail 2^-74.54 (declared; paired transfer arm -0.014 bit, s.e. 0.023). Memory 2^20.0000: peak over phases 1,013,513 bytes plus 32,768. Advice 160 bytes. Success 0.39.

heuristics.statement: For the selected-window distribution of the shipped program (KCAP=710, KTRY=32), the expected charged base-walk work per window is at most 472,362,354 operations and the distinct evaluated F9 claws per window are at most 910.38 on average, 0.015969 per distinct claw at the unit of 57,010.58 groups per window. Chaining values of random first blocks behave as independent uniform values for the walk map and the later events; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-entry count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11 do not depend on the chaining value; one-way ANOVA of 2,000 claws over 16 windows: entries F = 0.588, keys F = 0.564, on 15 and 1,984 df); at most 1,024 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (program cap, never reached in the 48 windows); W17 is uniform over claws and listed keys; survivors of the pass per evaluated claw are at most 0.23995 in expectation, the one-sided 99% bound of this entry's count on 48 full windows (10,114 survivors in 43,134 evaluated claws). The uniform model gives 62,400 x 2^-18 = 0.23804, shown for comparison.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and experiments/r39joint_k4.py with the shipped advice pair and the list generated at import.
heuristics.extrapolation: One-sided 99% bounds from this entry's own full windows of the shipped program: 24 for the base walk (mean 469,984,814, s.d. 4,659,006), 48 for the F9 claws (mean 898.62, s.d. 33.81) and G. Extended to 2^76.465113 windows by independence of first blocks.
heuristics.limitations: Samples of 24 and 48 windows on public seeds run by this entry; the organizer runs four windows of 2^21 evaluations of the same walk. Each premise at its own 99% bound.

heuristics.statement: The W17 pass costs exactly 143,633 operations per evaluated F9 claw: 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks), a formula of the table evaluated and asserted by the program, with no folded or claw-specialised code. A survivor costs 711 + 563 per class tested, at most 5,215; a key hit at most 49,472 (the at most 8 classes of its group as mates); the one-time setup, the rule generator included, is charged 1,107,473,556 operations. K = 10,719 is at least 1 percent above its formula.
heuristics.scope: The counted pass, survivor and key-hit paths and setup of experiments/r39joint_k4.py.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact counts of the program; the organizer run asserts the pass cost per claw and planted survivor costs.
heuristics.limitations: The 2^30 part of the setup is an allowance for the import's other statements.

heuristics.statement: For an F8-passing listed entry of the fibre 0x3cc9eebe drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, entry) triples of the attack (windows weighted by their trial count), in a claw passing F9 with W17 equal to the advice value (an entry the program compresses at every hit of its key), the two 39-step compressions give equal outputs along the advice differences with probability at least 2^-74.54. Measured directly by the entry-weighted arm J weighted by window size (participant-run, 28 organizer-protocol runs on F9 claws of the shipped program's windows): mean 2^-74.3828, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4928. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1). The declared bound QDECL of the shipped replica is 2^-74.54 (below its hard-asserted one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4326; 42 further runs: mean 2^-74.4434, 99.9% bound 2^-74.5296). Real variants of the new fibre do not lower it: paired joint arm against h0 variants, 28 organizer-protocol runs with identical SMC carrier, log2 ratio -0.014 (s.e. 0.023), one-sided 99% bound on the loss 0.071 bit; class-01-only -0.021. The key-weighted arm K on the same claws gives 2^-74.5058 weighted (99.9%), so the entry and key weightings agree.
heuristics.scope: Rows 18 to 38 of the advice trail after rows 0 to 17 hold; parity classes pooled as in 5f8e6192.
heuristics.extrapolation: Arm J draws (claw, entry) uniformly over F8-passing pairs on the shipped program's claws, the attack's trial weighting; every hit verified by recompressing both blocks. These arms are participant-run; the organizer's replica samples the advice distribution.
heuristics.limitations: The transfer is a 28-run arm, not a proof of equality; the attack's trials are all of class 01 (a0 even, W1 odd), whose paired figure is -0.021.

heuristics.statement: A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 are fixed to the advice values; (A[6], A[7]) range over the listed entries of the fibre 0x3cc9eebe; for every listed entry both messages follow the advice state-difference trail through step 15, W9 is C9 + 0x05cefde0 - a1 and W16 is one value per claw. Constructing and selecting the advice pair costs at most 2^43 compressions (2^42.545 by the accounting of proof Section 9), added to the claimed time; the offline fibre search costs at most about 2^31.1 compressions (estimated from the tools' loop counts), inside the remaining 2^41.1.
heuristics.scope: The one-time construction of the 160-byte advice pair of 5f8e6192; the list is generated at import by the rule of proof Section 2.5.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exhaustive enumeration over all 2^32 a3 with the real two-message trail checked on every entry at four points (0 failures); the rule reproduces that list exactly; the organizer run checks one entry of every group at the advice point.
heuristics.limitations: The 93-pair campaign was run by the pair's authors and is charged at its declared cost.

heuristics.statement: Windows are independent (fresh first blocks). Trials are listed entries passing F8 in a claw passing F9: at least 10598.2 per distinct claw, the one-sided 99% lower bound of this entry's count on 2,000 real F9 claws of the shipped program; W17 is shared by the mates of a key, so hits are counted on keys. Each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw (a uniform claw constant); events in different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of the shipped program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and family-wise over all keys E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 0.0078 (a third run of 65,536 random w; family-wise at 0.001 over all keys and the three runs). Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3 x 3,462,264 / 0.001) / 65,536 = 0.000352 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 65,536 w). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the mates' tail events, as for the hit events themselves. Real 2^-32 hits: 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over the 48 windows; 3 compressed F8-passing mates against 6.85 expected (P = 0.09, disclosed). The program tests every key hit; success is priced by second-order Bonferroni over all hits on the keys' mate-union events (proof Section 7), divisor 1 - 0.074784 (including the measured mate term of H7-mate-joint) with the cross-claw term bounded through the cap of 1,024 claws for any correlation; no premise between the tails of different hits is used.
heuristics.scope: The amplification over 2^76.465113 windows of the shipped program.
heuristics.extrapolation: F8-passing entries per F9 claw 682,518.4 (s.e. 1,205.5, 16 batches of 125 claws); per-claw s.d. 70,200; F9 claws per window from 48 windows.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run counts (2,000 claws, 48 windows). The organizer's dispersion test is a scaled spot test on four fixed groups; independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and windows is the premise, not a measurement.

heuristics.statement: For an F8-passing entry i whose pair collides along the advice differences (event T_i), the expected number of its other F8-passing mates on the same claw (same cv, a0, a1, a2; own a3) whose pairs follow the advice XOR differences through row 19 is at most eps = 3.086e-03: it is at most 7 (keys have at most 8 entries) times the probability that at least one does, which is at most 4.4092e-04. Hence sum over keys of P(U_k) >= (1 - eps/2) sum over entries of P(T_i), U_k the union of the key's mates' events, by second-order Bonferroni inside the key; eps/2 = 0.001544 is in the divisor. No independence between mates is assumed.
heuristics.scope: Every key hit: the program compresses every F8-passing mate (k4q); the bound is applied to every hit key of the attack.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the tail replica's conditional samples: arms M and J, 28 organizer-protocol ids each, 25,221 verified hits; every F8-passing mate of the hit entry (9,129, from an exhaustive mate index of the list) recompressed on the hit's own chaining value with k4_words; first deviation from the advice differences at row 18 for 4,735 and row 19 for 4,394, none later (0 hits with such a mate); design effect of SMC clustering priced at its one-sided 99% upper bound 1.608 (row-18 indicator, the largest of arm M, arm J and the two pooled per id; per-id pooled point value 0.767, M-J correlation +0.095); Kish factor 0.9986 on all hits; one-sided 99.9% Poisson bound for 0 events on 15,667 effective hits, times 7.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run (w16/tools/matejoint.py, w16/out/M_3cc9eebe.jsonl, J_3cc9eebe.jsonl, mate_stats.json). The replica samples claws through their words only; the bound is on following the advice differences through row 19, which contains the counted collision event.

heuristics.statement: Mean work per window is at most 605,977,191 operations against the cap 611,096,407 (margin 0.84%), and the per-window s.d. is at most 14,621,707, with each of the four sample moments at its one-sided 99.75% bound (99% jointly). For independent windows Chebyshev bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows below 7.9e-23.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 24 and 48 full windows of the shipped program.
heuristics.limitations: Normal-theory bounds on the sample moments.

heuristics.statement: Given the claws, the W17 events of distinct keys are dispersed as independent trials. Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event of probability 2^-7 on every key of four groups (every 50th) with an entry in F8, in every F9 claw of the four organizer windows: 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws; acceptance region fixed in the manifest and asserted.
heuristics.scope: Four of the 200 groups, all F9 claws of the four organizer windows of r39k4-window-small.
heuristics.extrapolation: The attack's event has probability 2^-32 on the same keys and words.
heuristics.limitations: Four groups only, for run time; the groups are fixed by the program.
